extracted.intended_audience: Entities participating in BOEM offshore renewable energy leasing and grants (bidders, prospective lessees, ROW/RUE applicants, and grant holders)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural criteria governing BOEM's competitive and noncompetitive leasing, auction procedures, bidding credits, post-auction obligations, lease/grant administration (assignments, consolidations, suspensions, relinquishments), ROW/RUE grants, and payments/financial assurance for offshore renewable energy activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN contents — requirements for performance under the lease
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for performance under the lease, including site-specific lease stipulations and environmental mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSN and FSN must describe site-specific obligations the lessee will have to perform under the lease (stipulations and mitigation).

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN contents — bidder eligibility steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps a bidder must take to ensure eligibility to participate in the auction (e.g., financial forms, bid deposits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSN/FSN should list required pre-auction steps, forms, and deposits bidders must complete to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN contents — availability and value of bidding credits
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability and potential value of bidding credit(s), if any are offered, and the actions or commitments required to obtain them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSN/FSN must explain whether bidding credits exist for the sale, how much they are worth (or how value is determined), and what commitments/actions are necessary to receive them.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN contents — auction format and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed description of the auction format and procedures as further described in § 585.223.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSN/FSN must describe the specific auction method, bidding rounds, rules, and procedural mechanics to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN contents — limits on number/sets of lease areas per bidder
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum number or specific sets of lease areas that any given bidder may be allowed to bid on or to acquire in an auction, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any limits on how many lease areas or which sets a bidder may seek must be stated in PSN/FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN contents — lease award procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Lease award procedures, including how and when a lease will be awarded and executed, and how BOEM will handle unsuccessful bids and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSN/FSN must explain award timing, execution steps, handling of unsuccessful bids, and post-auction administrative steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN contents — official BOEM lease form reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of, or a reference to, the official BOEM lease form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSN/FSN must include or reference the lease form that winning bidders will be required to sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN contents — other relevant matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Other relevant matters as determined by BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may include any additional information it deems relevant in the PSN/FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of competitive interest — Federal Register notice and comment
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may issue a notice in the Federal Register requesting information regarding competitive interest in an area and will consider respondents' comments to determine whether competitive interest remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When BOEM has reason to believe competitive interest no longer exists, it may solicit public input and rely on comments to evaluate continued competition; BOEM may end the competitive process if it determines competitive interest no longer exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when only a single party remains interested
rubrics_metrics.description: If only a single party remains interested in a lease area before auction, BOEM may proceed with the auction or with the noncompetitive process following payment by that party of the acquisition fee specified in § 585.502(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM has discretion to conduct the auction despite single interest or switch to noncompetitive issuance conditioned on acquisition fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: How bidding credits are evaluated in determining highest bid
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will determine the highest bid, taking into account the combined value of the monetary (cash) component and the non-monetary component(s) represented by bidding credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidding credits are treated as non-monetary components; combined cash plus credit value determines high bid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding credit disclosure in PSN/FSN
rubrics_metrics.description: The PSN and FSN will explain eligibility and application requirements, the value of each available bidding credit, and procedures for applying each available bidding credit to bids submitted during the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics on each bidding credit (eligibility, value—sum-certain or percentage of cash bid—and application procedures) must be provided in PSN/FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding credit eligibility timing and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for bidding credits must be established in advance of any lease auction and may be based on actions already undertaken or actions committed for the future, provided BOEM has agreed to terms by which such a commitment will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders must establish eligibility before the auction; commitments to future actions may qualify if BOEM accepts the terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors BOEM may offer bidding credits for
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may offer bidding credits for power purchase agreements; renewable energy credits or subsidies; development agreements facilitating shared transmission and grid interconnection; technical merit, timeliness, or financing and economic considerations; environmental considerations, public benefits, or compatibility with State and local needs; agreements facilitating OCS renewable energy development or other OCSLA goals; or any other factor identified in the PSN and FSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad non-exhaustive list of possible bases for bidding credits; PSN/FSN will specify which apply for each auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-auction establishment and BOEM determination of bidding credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the auction, bidders seeking to use bidding credits must establish that they meet the eligibility criteria and BOEM will determine each bidder's eligibility and the value of those bidding credits and inform each eligible bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM makes pre-auction determinations of eligibility and credit values and communicates them to bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment by provisional winner with bidding credits
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional winner who is awarded bidding credits must pay an amount equal to the cash component of its winning bid less any bid deposit retained by BOEM under § 585.501.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when bidding credits are applied to the bid, the winner must pay the cash portion net of retained deposit as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive award principle — fair, objective auction to highest bidder
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will award leases competitively using an objective, fair, reasonable, and competitive auction process that provides a fair return to the United States; leases will be awarded to the highest bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auction design must aim for objectivity and fair return; highest combined-value bidder wins subject to rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted auction methods
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may use any analog or digital method to conduct the auction; specific process and procedural details will be noticed in the PSN and finalized in the FSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility in technology and method, but PSN/FSN must specify chosen methods and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction triggers and FSN specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM determines competitive interest exists and decides to issue a lease, BOEM will conduct an auction; the auction's format, procedures, and other details will be specified in the FSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN is the operative document for auction mechanics once BOEM decides to proceed competitively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency procedures for auction malfunction
rubrics_metrics.description: The FSN will specify potential use of alternatives if the primary auction method, system, or mechanism malfunctions; BOEM may take alternate action consistent with § 585.221(d) until the malfunction is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN must set fallback mechanisms; BOEM may delay/suspend/cancel or restart auctions to preserve fairness and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM authority to delay, suspend or cancel auction
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time before a provisional winner is determined, BOEM may delay, suspend, or cancel an auction due to disaster, technical malfunction, security breach, unlawful bidding activity, administrative necessity, or any other reason BOEM determines may adversely affect fair and efficient conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM has broad discretion to interrupt auctions and restart or cancel them as appropriate to protect fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of provisional winner under FSN rules
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will determine the provisional winner for each lease area under the auction rules and bidding procedures prescribed in the FSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional winners are identified according to the FSN's prescribed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid deposit requirement to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidders must submit a deposit to participate in an auction under § 585.501, unless otherwise specified in the FSN; a provisional winner's bid deposit will be credited toward the balance due on its bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit amounts/process are specified in FSN and are a condition of participation and partial payment for winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder qualification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Only bidders qualified by BOEM under §§ 585.106 and 585.107 are permitted to bid during an auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders must meet BOEM's qualification criteria prior to participation; FSN may reference these prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized agent designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an authorized agent may act on a bidder's behalf during an auction; bidders must submit the names of their authorized agents to BOEM before the auction, as prescribed in the FSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation during auctions requires prior notification and authorization as set forth in FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow FSN auction process and prohibition on disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bidder must follow the auction process specified in the FSN and may not take any action to disrupt or alter the process beyond its intended function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders must adhere strictly to FSN rules and avoid behaviors that would distort or interfere with the auction mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify BOEM of inability to submit bid
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder is responsible for immediately contacting BOEM if it is unable to submit its bid for any reason during an auction; failure to timely notify BOEM may preclude disputing the auction or lease award on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely communication is required; BOEM may pause, use alternatives, or continue without the affected bidder at its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on bidder collusion/disclosure of strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidders may not disclose their auction strategies or economic valuations of a lease area to other bidders listed in the FSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality of competitive strategies is required to prevent collusion and protect competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN supplemental information — bidding instructions and systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidding instructions, procedures, and systems, including the bid variables — how the auction will be conducted and what systems and procedures will be utilized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN must provide operational details about bidding formats, variables, and technical systems employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN supplemental information — bid deposit amount and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Bid deposit — the amount a bidder must pay under § 585.501 to be eligible to bid and the FSN-prescribed process and deadline for submitting a bid deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN will specify exact deposit amounts and submission deadlines/processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN supplemental information — mock auction
rubrics_metrics.description: Mock auction — notice of a practice auction before the actual auction; only bidders eligible for the actual auction will be permitted to participate in the mock (i.e., practice) auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may offer a practice run to familiarize eligible bidders with procedures and systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN supplemental information — auction date/time/location
rubrics_metrics.description: Auction date, starting time and location — including relevant time zone and where the auction will take place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN must state when and where the auction occurs and time-zone details for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN supplemental information — minimum bid
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum bid — the price at which the bidding will start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN clarifies the floor price for bidding initiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN supplemental information — information released between rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Information BOEM will release to bidders between rounds — may include prior round results and other updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN must specify what bidder information (e.g., standings) will be disclosed during multi-round auctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN supplemental information — tie-breaking provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Tie-breaking provision — method BOEM will use to break a tie between identical high bids for the same lease area or package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN must specify the mechanism to resolve identical high bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN/FSN supplemental information — next highest bidder
rubrics_metrics.description: Next highest bidder — method BOEM will use to determine the next highest bidder if the provisional winner fails to meet obligations or a competitively issued lease is relinquished/cancelled within six months of the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN must provide procedures for replacing a provisional winner or reoffering relinquished parcels, including pricing methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-auction review and bid disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: At conclusion BOEM will declare bidding closed; assess whether bids meet requirements of regulations and the FSN; BOEM may disqualify bids based on this review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-auction administrative compliance review may lead to disqualification for failure to meet regulatory or FSN criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust review of lease sale results
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 43 U.S.C. 1337(c), BOEM will provide DOJ, in consultation with FTC, opportunity to conduct an antitrust review of lease sale results and may disqualify bids based on results of this review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lease awards are subject to interagency antitrust scrutiny which can affect award validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM acceptance/rejection timing and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will accept or reject bids within 90 calendar days of auction closure; BOEM may extend that time by notice to bidders within 15 calendar days before the 90-calendar day period ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM has a 90-day decision window (subject to notice of extension) to formally accept or reject auction bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds and written explanations for rejected bids
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will deem rejected any bid not accepted within the 90-calendar-day period or any extension and will provide each rejected bidder a written explanation and refund any monies deposited without interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejected bidders receive explanation and return of deposits (no interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of lease area between auction closure and execution
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may withdraw all or part of a lease area from the lease sale between auction closure and lease execution; if portion is withdrawn, provisional winner may refuse without penalty, propose new lease terms, or accept reduced area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM retains post-auction control to reduce or withdraw acreage with options afforded to the provisional winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-auction and restarting competitive process
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may re-auction unsold lease areas at conclusion of auction and may restart the competitive leasing process at any point in § 585.210 it deems reasonable and appropriate (e.g., RFI, Call, area identification, PSN, or FSN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsold or retracted areas can be reintroduced via any appropriate stage of the leasing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional winner obligations upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will identify and notify the provisional winner of amount due (cash component less bid deposit) and provide three unsigned copies of the lease; within 10 business days the provisional winner must execute all three copies, file financial assurance as required, and pay the amount due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict post-acceptance deadlines and financial assurance filing requirements attach to provisional winners; extensions possible at BOEM's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM execution of lease and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will execute the lease after the provisional winner completes the requirements and any timely appeals have been resolved; after execution, provisional winner becomes winning bidder and BOEM will send one fully executed copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lease is not effective until BOEM signs following satisfaction of requirements and resolution of appeals; executed lease triggers subsequent payment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of first 12 months' rent by winning bidder
rubrics_metrics.description: The winning bidder must pay the first 12 months' rent under § 585.503(a) within 45-calendar days after receiving a copy of the executed lease from BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-year rent has a 45-day post-execution payment deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repayment requirement if lessee fails bidding credit commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lessee does not meet the commitments it made to obtain any bidding credits, the lessee will be required to repay the value of the bidding credits received, adjusted for inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidding credits are conditional; failure to fulfill related commitments triggers repayment with inflation adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for provisional winner failure to meet obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional winner fails to timely complete required steps or comply with laws/regulations/FSN provisions, BOEM may decline to execute the lease, decline to execute leases for other areas the provisional winner won, require forfeiture of bid deposit (limited if deposit exceeds winning bid), refer for suspension/debarment review, or pursue any other remedy available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM has a palette of remedies including declination, forfeiture, debarment referral, and other remedies; forfeiture limited to amount of winning bid if deposit exceeds bid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for selecting new provisional winner after failure
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM declines to execute a lease with the provisional winner, BOEM may select a new provisional winner by repeating the auction, selecting the next highest bid, or using other FSN-specified procedures; decisions are appealable under § 585.118(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement selection follows FSN-provided procedures or re-auction; decisions are subject to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompetitive lease issuance criteria — unsolicited requests
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will consider unsolicited requests for a lease on a case-by-case basis and may issue a lease noncompetitively only if it has determined after public notice that no competitive interest exists; BOEM will not consider an unsolicited request in a lease area scheduled for auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompetitive issuance is an exception triggered by a formal no-competitive-interest determination and excluded when an auction is scheduled for an area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RFI for unsolicited lease requests
rubrics_metrics.description: At BOEM's discretion, BOEM may issue an RFI relating to your unsolicited lease request and will consider comments received to determine if competitive interest exists; if BOEM decides not to issue an RFI and not to continue processing your request, it will refund your acquisition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFI serves as a tool to assess competition; lack of RFI may trigger refund of acquisition fee if BOEM stops processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of finding competitive interest on unsolicited request
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM determines competitive interest exists in the lease area, BOEM will proceed with competitive process; if you submit a bid, acquisition fee applies to deposit for bonus bid; if you do not submit a bid, BOEM will not refund acquisition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition fee may be credited to competitive deposit if you bid; otherwise it is nonrefundable once competitive process proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: No competitive interest determination — fees and environmental review
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM determines no competitive interest and further investigation is in public interest, BOEM will publish determination and provide a written estimate of proposed fee to pay for processing costs including any environmental review required before lease issuance; BOEM will conduct required environmental reviews and consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompetitive issuance may require the applicant to pay processing and environmental review costs as estimated by BOEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines after determination of no competitive interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 calendar days of receiving the written estimate of the fee (or longer as determined by BOEM) you must pay the fee for any environmental review; failure to pay may result in withdrawal of the determination. A determination of no competitive interest expires two years after publication unless extended for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must timely pay review fees and be prepared for the two-year expiration limit subject to BOEM discretion to extend or withdraw for lack of due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: CZMA consistency certification responsibility after no competitive interest
rubrics_metrics.description: After BOEM publishes the determination of no competitive interest, you are responsible for submitting any consistency certification and necessary data to the applicable State CZMA agencies and BOEM pursuant to 15 CFR part 930, subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompetitive applicants must handle Coastal Zone Management Act consistency processes with states and BOEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompetitive lease acceptance obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you accept the terms and conditions of the lease, BOEM will issue the lease and you must, within 10 business days after receiving the lease copies, execute all three copies and file financial assurance as required; you must pay the first 12 months' rent no later than 45 calendar days after receiving executed lease copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompetitive winners have the same execution, financial assurance, and initial rent deadlines as competitive winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of not accepting or failing financial assurance for noncompetitive lease
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not accept the terms in a timely manner or do not comply with financial assurance requirements, BOEM may decide not to issue a lease and will not refund your acquisition fee or any fees paid under the environmental review fee requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely accept or meet assurance requirements can result in loss of fee amounts and non-issuance of lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial lease periods — preliminary period
rubrics_metrics.description: Each commercial lease has a preliminary period of up to five years during which the lessee must submit a COP; preliminary period begins on effective date and ends when COP received or at five years, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary period provides time to prepare a COP; submission ends preliminary period earlier if timely submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial lease periods — COP review period and lessee obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: COP review period begins when BOEM receives a COP and ends upon approval, disapproval, or approval with modifications; during the COP review period BOEM conducts necessary reviews and the lessee must resolve issues identified as incomplete within the first year of the COP review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee must address BOEM-identified incompleteness promptly (within first year) during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial lease periods — design and construction period
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and construction period is for the duration specified in the approved COP (may be modified by mutual agreement); during this period the lessee must submit FDR and FIR, address BOEM issues, and complete project construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-approval milestones and filings (FDR/FIR) and construction completion are tied to COP-specified schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial lease periods — operations period
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations period is 30 years or duration specified in the lease; begins with start of commercial operations and may be extended by suspension, lease extension, or renewal as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee's commercial operations duration and mechanisms to add time are defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting extension of lease periods
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request an extension of any lease period for good cause; BOEM may approve in its discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are discretionary and require demonstration of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased development lease period scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: If intending to develop your lease in phases, you may propose lease period schedules appropriate for each phase in your COP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COP may include phased timelines for COP/Construction/Operations to match phased development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited lease preliminary period and GAP requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each limited lease has a preliminary period of 12 months to submit a GAP; if BOEM receives a GAP that satisfies §§ 585.640–585.648, the preliminary period will be automatically extended for time necessary to conduct a technical and environmental review; the GAP must meet those requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited leases have shorter preliminary period but submission of acceptable GAP triggers automatic review extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROW grant width and relinquishment option
rubrics_metrics.description: ROW grants should be of a width sufficient to accommodate potential changes at design and installation phases, with an option for the grant holder to relinquish unused portions after construction is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ROW design must anticipate flexibility; relinquishment of unused ROW portions is permitted post-construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area limits for associated facilities under ROW/RUE
rubrics_metrics.description: For associated facilities, area is limited to what is reasonably necessary for a power or pumping station or other requested facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated facility footprints are restricted to reasonable minimum necessary areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROW/RUE applicant qualification evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: To acquire a ROW grant or RUE grant an applicant must provide evidence that they meet the qualifications set forth in §§ 585.106 and 585.107.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate compliance with BOEM qualification standards analogous to lease bidders/lessees.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROW/RUE grant periods — preliminary and operations periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ROW or RUE grant has a preliminary period of 12 months to submit a GAP; each has an operations period set by BOEM or negotiated, which begins on the date BOEM approves the GAP; extensions may be requested for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeframes mirror limited-lease structure with preliminary GAP submission and operations period tied to GAP approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROW/RUE request submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for new or modified ROW or RUE grants must be submitted to BOEM pursuant to § 585.110; a separate request is required for each grant requested and the request must contain specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each ROW/RUE requires its own application package following BOEM's § 585.110 procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process when BOEM determines no competitive interest for ROW/RUE
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM determines there is no competitive interest in a ROW or RUE grant, BOEM will publish a notice; after publication the applicant is responsible for submitting required consistency certifications and data to BOEM and applicable State CZMA agency and BOEM may establish terms and offer the grant to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompetitive ROW/RUE issuance follows similar notice, CZMA, and offer/acceptance mechanics as leases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalties for noncompliance and conditions for assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may assess civil penalties as authorized by section 24 of the OCS Lands Act and as determined under 30 CFR part 550, subpart N, if you fail to comply with any provision of this part or any term of a lease, grant, or order: (1) after notice and expiration of a reasonable corrective period; or (2) without notice if BOEM determines the failure may constitute a threat of serious, irreparable, or immediate harm or damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties may be assessed following notice and cure period or immediately for threats of serious harm; reference to procedural regulations for penalty assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator designation requirement in SAP/COP/GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: If you intend to designate an operator who is not the lessee or grant holder, you must identify the proposed operator in your SAP, COP, or GAP as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator identity must be disclosed in the applicable project or plan submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment application format and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may assign a lease or grant interest by submitting one paper copy and one electronic copy of an assignment application to BOEM, Form BOEM-0003 for leases and Form BOEM-0002 for grants; assignment is not needed for business mergers, name changes, or changes of business form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment requires specific forms and dual-format submission; routine corporate changes do not require assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an assignment results in a segregated lease
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is an assignment by all record title owners of 100 percent of the record title to one or more aliquots in a lease, the assigned and retained portions become segregated into separate and distinct leases; financial assurance requirements apply separately to each segregated lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-title aliquot transfers cause segregation with separate obligations and assurance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of transferring an undivided interest less than 100%
rubrics_metrics.description: If a record title owner transfers an undivided interest of less than 100 percent of the record title interest in any given aliquot, that transfer will not segregate the aliquot but create joint ownership between assignee and assignor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial undivided transfers create joint owners rather than separate segregated leases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee liability — compliance with lease/grant terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees are bound to comply with each term or condition of the lease or grant and the regulations in this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning parties remain subject to the same regulatory and contractual obligations as original lessees/grant holders insofar as assignee is concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation application and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply to consolidate all or part of two or more adjacent leases or grants held by the same lessee or grant holder into one new lease or grant; application must include description and identifiers; an approved consolidation creates a new lease subject to the terms and conditions of the consolidated leases and grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation requires BOEM approval, documentation of impacted leases/blocks/aliquots, and results in a new instrument carrying applicable terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default rules for consolidation — time remaining and other terms
rubrics_metrics.description: If consolidated leases/grants have different remaining times, BOEM will default to using the shorter remaining periods in the new lease but will consider extension requests; if they have different terms and conditions, BOEM will default to terms in the most recently issued leases/grants for the new lease but may consider modifications for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation favors the more restrictive (shorter) schedules and the most recent terms, subject to BOEM discretion to modify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assurance assessment for consolidations
rubrics_metrics.description: Before approving consolidation BOEM will assess appropriate financial assurance obligations for the new lease or grant per §§ 585.516 and 585.517 or §§ 585.520 and 585.521.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial assurance will be recalculated/required for consolidated instruments consistent with subpart F requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of suspension on lease/grant expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspension extends the expiration date for the relevant period of your lease or grant for the length of time the suspension is in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspensions pause the running of lease/grant periods for the suspension duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension request contents and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a written request for suspension no later than 90 calendar days before expiration including reasons, length of additional time requested, explanation why suspension is in public interest, and any other information BOEM may require; if unable to timely submit COP or GAP you may request suspension with a revised schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension petitions require substantive justification and timeliness, and may be used to extend preliminary periods for plan preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to furnish study results to BOEM under suspension order authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM orders a suspension under certain authorities you must furnish a copy of the study and results to BOEM pursuant to § 585.110.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research/study materials supporting suspension requests or orders must be submitted to BOEM per procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver or deferral of payments during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM approves your request for a suspension or orders one, BOEM may waive or defer your payment obligations during the suspension depending on the reasons for suspension and your responsibility for the circumstances necessitating a suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment relief during suspension is discretionary and conditioned on cause and lessee responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal request timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For commercial leases, requests for renewal must be submitted no later than two years before the termination date of the operations period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessees must plan early and submit renewal applications at least two years before operations period end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of renewal determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will set the length of renewal on a case-by-case basis; for commercial leases it will not exceed the original operations period unless a longer time is negotiated, and for limited leases it will not exceed the original operations period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal lengths are capped at original durations except by negotiation for commercial leases; BOEM discretion applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors BOEM will consider in deciding whether to renew
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will consider criteria set forth in § 585.429 and may consider other relevant factors as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal decisions weigh multiple statutory and regulatory factors plus any other relevant considerations BOEM deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: When lease/grant terminates
rubrics_metrics.description: A lease or grant terminates on expiration of the applicable period unless extended for good cause, a renewal request is pending, or lease/grant is suspended or renewed, in which case it terminates on the date set forth in the notice of suspension or renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination timing depends on pending actions (extensions, renewals, suspensions) and BOEM notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment procedure and continuing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: You may surrender a lease or grant or designated subdivision by filing a properly completed official relinquishment form; relinquishment takes effect on date BOEM receives the completed form, subject to continued obligations to make payments due, decommission facilities to BOEM's satisfaction, and perform other outstanding obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relinquishment does not absolve past or continuing obligations; ONRR will bill for any outstanding payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of relinquished/contracted/cancelled parcels
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lease or grant (or portion) is relinquished, contracted, or cancelled, BOEM may restart the competitive leasing process at any appropriate point subject to environmental analyses and consultations; competitively issued parcels relinquished/cancelled within six months of auction may be reoffered to next highest bidder at next best bid or prorated amount reflecting fair return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-relinquishment measures include reoffering, reauctioning, or restarting the leasing pipeline; pricing for reoffers aims to ensure fair return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic payment mechanism for acquisition/initial rent
rubrics_metrics.description: For acquisition fees or the initial 12 months' rent paid for the preliminary period of your lease, you must make electronic payments through the Fees for Services page on the BOEM website and include a Pay.gov confirmation receipt with your unsolicited request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified online payment portal and proof of payment are required for initial fee transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment schedule and amounts for initial and subsequent lease payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial payments: bid deposit as set in Final Sale Notice (with bid); bonus balance due within 10 business days of receiving unsigned lease; acquisition fee $0.25 per acre with application for noncompetitive leases; initial rent $3 per acre per year due 45 calendar days after lease execution. Subsequent payments include annual rent and operating fees as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN/Final Sale Notice set some payment amounts/timing; there are standard statutory/reserved amounts (e.g., $3/acre initial rent) and payment mechanics tied to execution timelines.
